title: Geometric HRV, cross-tool: the triangular index (HTI) bit-for-bit vs NeuroKit2 (and the TINN convention)

dataset.name: Fantasia Database
dataset.record: record f1y01 (young healthy subject), a 5-minute RR-interval series (391 intervals, ms)
dataset.citation: Iyengar N, Peng CK, Morin R, Goldberger AL, Lipsitz LA. Age-related alterations in the fractal scaling of cardiac interbeat interval dynamics. Am J Physiol 1996;271(4):R1078-R1084. Fantasia Database, PhysioNet (Goldberger et al. 2000).

proposition: The HRV triangular index (HTI) and TINN are the Task-Force geometric HRV measures, prized for artifact robustness. The ecosystem ships ecgHRVgeometric but it had never been cross-checked against the field-standard NeuroKit2. On a real 5-minute Fantasia RR series HTI reproduces NeuroKit2 hrv_time HRV_HTI BIT-FOR-BIT (|diff| 0) -- an integer-ratio index (391 intervals / a modal histogram height of 35 = 11.17). TINN, by contrast, differs (164 vs 297 ms), a documented triangular-interpolation convention difference (least-squares triangle base width vs NeuroKit2's fit), not a bug in either tool.

claims.statement: HRV triangular index (HTI) of the Fantasia RR series
modal (peak) NN-histogram count -- the denominator of HTI
NN interval count -- the numerator of HTI (HTI = n / modal count)
TINN (triangular interpolation of the NN histogram) from ecgHRVgeometric (ms)
|TINN op - NeuroKit2 TINN| -- a documented triangular-interpolation convention difference

validation.reference: The shipped ecgHRVgeometric op is validated against the field-standard NeuroKit2 hrv_time geometric indices on the identical Fantasia RR series. HTI (the triangular index) reproduces NeuroKit2 HRV_HTI BIT-FOR-BIT (|diff| 0): it is an integer-ratio index (391 intervals / a modal histogram height of 35) at the shared 1/128 s standard bin. TINN differs (164 vs 297 ms), a documented triangular-interpolation convention difference.
validation.data: REAL -- Fantasia (PhysioNet), record f1y01, 5-minute RR series (391 intervals)
validation.note: The reproducible findings are (1) HTI reproduces NeuroKit2 HRV_HTI bit-for-bit (|diff| 0); (2) TINN differs by 133 ms, a triangular-interpolation convention. HONEST scope: (1) this is a CROSS-TOOL re-certification of a shipped op (ecgHRVgeometric, extended here only to accept an RR data frame), NOT new-method authoring; (2) HTI is a genuine BIT-FOR-BIT match -- an integer-ratio index (n intervals / modal count) at the shared 1/128 s standard bin, so once the bin width matches the value is unambiguous and the residual is exactly zero, not a convention agreement; (3) TINN, by contrast, DIFFERS (164 vs 297 ms), a documented triangular-interpolation CONVENTION difference, not a bug in either tool: ecgHRVgeometric takes the least-squares triangle base width, NeuroKit2 uses a different triangular fit; this is surfaced honestly, not hidden; (4) HTI is the more robust and portable of the two (a dimensionless integer ratio), which is exactly why it cross-validates cleanly while TINN does not; (5) run_simulation = FALSE (deterministic).

open_questions.q: TINN's cross-tool divergence is a convention choice worth standardizing: reporting both the least-squares base width and the triangle-fit variant (or the histogram's coefficient-of-variation / TINN-M) would let users reconcile TINN across toolchains, as this case does for HTI. Documented, not escalated.
